mainTopic: אימורין of a פסח brought בטומאה, and the differences between פסח מצרים and פסח דורות
overview: This amud opens by finishing a question about a קרבן פסח brought בטומאה, where the meat may be eaten even by impure people. רבא rules that impure people who eat the אימורין are not liable either, because the אימורין rule is learned from the meat rule. רבי זירא then asks where the אימורין of פסח מצרים were burned. אביי answers that they may simply have been roasted and eaten, since the doorframe was the only 'altar' in מצרים. A new משנה lists how פסח מצרים differed from פסח דורות: it was taken on the tenth, its blood was put on the doorframe with hyssop, and it was eaten in haste. The גמרא learns from the word הזה that taking on the tenth applied only in מצרים. It then tests that method against many פסוקים: eating at night, the ערל, the בן נכר, the תושב and שכיר, household מילה, breaking a bone, and eating raw. Each time, ועבדת את העבודה הזאת carries the rule to all generations, and the limiting word (הזה, בו, ממנו) is given a different job. Eating in haste stays only for מצרים because of the word אותו. The amud ends by asking what 'פסח דורות applies all seven days' refers to, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does permitting impure meat also permit impure sacrificial portions?
steps.stepSummary: In a פסח brought בטומאה, the meat may be eaten while impure. The גמרא asks whether that permission also covers impure people who eat the אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Since eating the meat while impure was permitted, was eating the sacrificial portions while impure also permitted? Or perhaps what was permitted is permitted, and what was not permitted stays not permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question with two sides. It wants to know whether the permission to eat impure meat in a פסח שבא בטומאה spreads to the אימורין too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side says the permission for the meat carries over to the אימורין. The second side says only the meat was specifically permitted. The אימורין stay under the normal כרת rule for eating קדשים בטומאה.

was permitted

steps.confusionAlert: The case started on the previous amud. We are talking about a פסח brought while the community is impure. In that special case the meat is eaten בטומאה. We are not talking about a normal קרבן.

steps.title: רבא shows that the law of the portions comes from the law of the meat
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out where the rule comes from. The liability for eating אימורין בטומאה is learned from the liability for meat, through the words אשר לה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: After all, from where do we include the impurity rule for sacrificial portions? From the impurity rule for meat. It is written 'that belong to ה׳,' to include the sacrificial portions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer by naming the source of the אימורין rule. The source is a פסוק about meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pasuk about כרת for eating impure meat adds the words 'אשר לה׳'. Those words include the אימורין. So the אימורין rule is not an independent law. It is attached to the meat law and depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: after all, consider (opens a reasoning)
was included (by a pasuk)
'that belong to ה׳‎' (ויקרא ז:כ)
to include

phrases.english: Rava said:

steps.title: Where the meat has no liability, the portions have none either
steps.stepSummary: Because the אימורין rule comes from the meat rule, the two always go together. Wherever there is liability for impure meat, there is liability for impure אימורין. Wherever there is none for meat, there is none for אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever the impurity rule applies to meat, it applies to the sacrificial portions. Wherever the impurity rule does not apply to meat, it does not apply to the sacrificial portions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer with a general rule. The rule settles the question: in a פסח שבא בטומאה, there is no liability for eating the אימורין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a פסח שבא בטומאה, eating the meat while impure carries no liability. The אימורין law grows out of the meat law. So the אימורין also carry no liability there. This decides the question in favor of the first side.

keyTerms.meaning: wherever
it exists / applies
it does not exist / does not apply

steps.whatToRemember: A rule learned from another rule is tied to it. When the main rule (meat) doesn't apply, the added rule (אימורין) doesn't apply either. So impure people who eat the אימורין of a פסח שבא בטומאה are not liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: something derived through a ריבוי follows the scope of its source.

phrases.english: Wherever there is liability for impurity of the meat,
there is liability for impurity of the sacrificial portions.
Wherever there is no liability for impurity of the meat,
there is no liability for impurity of the sacrificial portions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical rule from the source given in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No liability for eating the אימורין of a פסח שבא בטומאה while impure, since there is none for the meat.

steps.title: Where were the portions of פסח מצרים burned?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks a new question. Where did the Jews burn the אימורין of the פסח they brought in מצרים? There was no altar there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: The sacrificial portions of the פסח in Egypt, where did they burn them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. רבי זירא asks what was done with the altar portions of the very first פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the אימורין of a פסח must be burned on the מזבח. The Torah never mentions an altar in מצרים. So רבי זירא asks where those parts were burned.

keyTerms.meaning: asked (a real question of law)
the first פסח, brought in Egypt before the Exodus
did they burn them (as an offering)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
The sacrificial portions of the Paschal lamb of Egypt —
where did they burn them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about פסח מצרים, still connected to the theme of אימורין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where were the אימורין of פסח מצרים burned, with no מזבח available?

steps.title: אביי suggests they may have simply roasted and eaten them
steps.stepSummary: אביי questions the starting assumption of the question. Who says the אימורין were burned at all? Maybe they roasted them and ate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And who tells us that they did not make them roasted (and eat them)?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by asking a question back. He suggests the אימורין in מצרים were never burned, but roasted and eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא assumed the אימורין of פסח מצרים had to be burned. אביי rejects that assumption. The laws of קרבנות had not yet been given. So the whole animal may have been roasted and eaten (per the ערוך's explanation of שויסקי).

keyTerms.meaning: and who will tell us? (challenges an assumption)
roasted food (per the ערוך)
they made / did

steps.confusionAlert: This sounds like a question, but it is really an answer. אביי is saying: don't assume they burned the אימורין at all.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And who will tell us
that they did not make them roasted (and eat them)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּמַאן לֵימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי זירא by rejecting the assumption behind his question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Maybe the אימורין were not burned at all, but roasted and eaten.

steps.title: רב יוסף's teaching: the doorframe was the only altar in Egypt
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a second support. רב יוסף taught that in מצרים the only 'altars' were the lintel and the two doorposts, and there was nothing else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further, רב יוסף taught: there were three altars there: on the lintel and on the two doorposts. And there was nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second support for his answer to רבי זירא, a ברייתא of רב יוסף. In מצרים, the doorframe served as the 'altar' for the blood, and no other altar existed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא asked where the אימורין were burned in מצרים. אביי already said that maybe they were not burned at all. Now he adds proof: the only 'altars' were the three parts of the doorframe, and those were used only for the blood. So there was nowhere to burn the fats, which fits the idea that they were roasted and eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which introduces an additional argument
Altars

Doorposts, the two side beams of the doorframe
And nothing more

steps.whatToRemember: In מצרים the doorframe was the 'altar,' used only for the blood. There was no altar to burn the אימורין, so they were likely roasted and eaten.

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rav Yosef taught:
phrases.notes: A second support for אביי's answer

phrases.english: There were three altars there (in Egypt):
On the lintel, and on the two doorposts.
phrases.notes: The places where the blood was put took the place of an altar

phrases.english: And there was nothing else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a source-based support to אביי's answer in step 5

steps.title: משנה: differences between פסח מצרים and פסח דורות
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists how פסח מצרים differed from פסח דורות. It was bought on the tenth, its blood was sprinkled with hyssop on the doorframe, it was eaten in haste, and its observance lasted one night, while the later פסח applies for seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between the פסח of מצרים and the פסח of the generations? The פסח of מצרים was taken from the tenth of the month. It needed sprinkling with a bundle of hyssop, on the lintel and on the two doorposts. It was eaten in haste, in one night. And the פסח of the generations applies all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the special rules that applied only to the very first פסח in מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is something that happened in מצרים but does not apply in later years: buying the lamb four days early, hyssop, blood on the doorframe, and eating in a rush. The last contrast, 'one night' versus 'seven days,' is unclear on its face. The גמרא will discuss its meaning later.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח brought in מצרים on the night of the Exodus
The קרבן פסח of all later generations
Its purchase (or selection) was from the tenth of ניסן
A bundle of hyssop, used to apply the blood
In haste

steps.confusionAlert: 'One night' versus 'seven days' does not mean the later פסח was eaten for a week. The קרבן is always eaten on one night. The גמרא later explains what this contrast refers to.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
What is the difference between the Pesach of Egypt
and the Pesach of the generations?
The Pesach of Egypt was taken from the tenth (of Nisan),
and it required sprinkling with a bundle of hyssop,
and on the lintel and on the two doorposts,
and it was eaten in haste, in one night.
phrases.notes: The גמרא later explains the 'one night' contrast

phrases.english: And the Pesach of the generations applies all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is related in theme, since it continues the topic of פסח מצרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פסח מצרים had unique rules: taken on the tenth, hyssop, blood on the doorframe, eaten in haste, observed one night. פסח דורות applies for seven days.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source showing that the משנה's special rules applied only to פסח מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for a source. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה claimed these rules were special to מצרים. The גמרא wants to see where the תורה limits them, starting with buying the lamb on the tenth.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Gemara:
From where do we know this?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that taking the lamb on the tenth applied only to פסח מצרים

steps.title: The word 'this' limits taking on the tenth to Egypt
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'on the tenth of this month they shall take.' The word הזה ('this') teaches that only this פסח, the one in מצרים, was taken on the tenth, and not the later ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Speak to the whole congregation of Israel, saying: on the tenth of this month they shall take.' This one is taken from the tenth, but the פסח of the generations is not taken from the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about taking the lamb on the tenth. It reads the word 'this' as a limiting word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'of this month' are read as pointing only to that specific time in מצרים. So the rule of taking the lamb four days early was a one-time rule, and later generations do not need it.

keyTerms.meaning: On the tenth of the month
'This,' read here as a limiting word
And they shall take

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Speak to the whole congregation of Israel, saying:
phrases.notes: שמות יב:ג

phrases.english: on the tenth of this month they shall take.'
phrases.notes: The word הזה is the key

phrases.english: This one is taken from the tenth,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word הזה in שמות יב:ג limits taking on the tenth to פסח מצרים

steps.title: Challenge: then the four-day inspection should also be only for Egypt
steps.stepSummary: If הזה limits a rule to מצרים, then the next פסוק, 'guard it until the fourteenth of this month,' should also limit the four-day inspection to מצרים alone. Yet the גמרא is not ready to say that inspection is needed only there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so: 'And it shall be guarded for you until the fourteenth day of this month.' Should we also say that this one needs inspection for four days before slaughter, and no other needs inspection?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading it just gave. The same word הזה appears in the פסוק about guarding the lamb, and that would lead to a result the גמרא finds hard to accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Guarding the lamb from the tenth to the fourteenth means checking it for blemishes for four days. If הזה always means 'only in מצרים,' this inspection would also be limited to מצרים. The גמרא treats that as a problem, so the proof from הזה is now in question.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now (the opening of a challenge from the logic just used)
For guarding (keeping the animal under watch)
Inspecting the animal for blemishes
So too, should we say the same here?

'And it shall be guarded for you
phrases.notes: שמות יב:ו

phrases.aramaic: עַד אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה״,
phrases.english: until the fourteenth day of this month,'
phrases.notes: The same word הזה appears here

phrases.english: so too, should we say:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה טָעוּן בִּיקּוּר אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים קוֹדֶם שְׁחִיטָה,

phrases.notes: The גמרא treats this result as unacceptable

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that הזה limits a rule to פסח מצרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word הזה appears in the פסוק about guarding the lamb until the fourteenth. The same reading would wrongly limit the four-day inspection to מצרים.

steps.title: בן בג בג: Even the תמיד needs a four-day inspection, learned from פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of בן בג בג teaches that the קרבן תמיד must be inspected four days before slaughter. He learns this from the פסח through the shared idea of 'guarding'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: בן בג בג says, how do we know the תמיד needs to be checked four days before it is slaughtered? The פסוק about the תמיד says 'you shall guard it to offer to Me in its time,' and about the פסח it says 'it shall be guarded for you until the fourteenth.' Just as the פסח needs four days of checking before slaughter, so does the תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge from step 10 with a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows that the four-day inspection is so basic that even the תמיד learns it from the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the גמרא doubted that the four-day inspection applied only in מצרים. Now it brings proof: if the תמיד, which is offered every day for all generations, learns inspection from the פסח, then inspection is clearly not a one-time rule for מצרים. So the word הזה cannot be limiting inspection to פסח מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering brought every morning and afternoon in the בית המקדש
Inspection: checking the animal for blemishes (מומים) before it is offered
'You shall guard.' This word is used for the תמיד and links it to the פסח
Guarding or keeping. Used for the פסח: 'it shall be guarded for you until the fourteenth'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this ברייתא is about the פסח itself. It is about the תמיד. The גמרא uses it to show that the פסח's inspection rule is strong enough to spread to another קרבן, so it can hardly be limited to מצרים alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the הלכה that the תמיד lambs must be inspected four days before they are offered.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Ben Bag Bag says:
From where do we know that the daily offering requires inspection
four days before slaughter?
As it says: 'You shall guard it to offer to Me in its time,'
phrases.notes: במדבר כח:ב, about the תמיד

phrases.english: and there (about the פסח) it says:
'And it shall be guarded for you until the fourteenth,'
phrases.notes: שמות יב:ו, about the פסח

phrases.english: just as there it requires inspection
four days before slaughter,
so too here it requires inspection
four days before slaughter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ברייתא to support the challenge in step 10, showing that inspection is not limited to פסח מצרים.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the four-day inspection cannot be limited to פסח מצרים alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of בן בג בג: the תמיד learns four-day inspection from the פסח through the shared language of guarding (תשמרו / משמרת).

steps.title: The תמיד is different because it has the word תשמרו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תמיד's inspection comes from its own word תשמרו. So the ברייתא does not prove that every פסח needs inspection.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written 'תשמרו' (you shall guard).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof from בן בג בג. The תמיד gets inspection because of its own special word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד has the word תשמרו, which creates a גזירה שוה to the פסח מצרים. A גזירה שוה can copy a rule even from a one-time case like פסח מצרים. So the ברייתא does not show that the פסח inspection is a rule for all generations, and הזה could still limit it to מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. The case being compared has a special feature
As it is written. Points to a specific פסוק
Learning a law from one topic to another through a shared word in the תורה

phrases.english: It is different there,
since it is written: 'You shall guard.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the proof from בן בג בג's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (אוקימתא of the source): the תמיד has its own textual basis.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the תמיד learns inspection from the פסח, the inspection must be a lasting rule for every פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תמיד's inspection rests on its own word תשמרו, so it proves nothing about whether later פסחים need inspection.

steps.title: פסח דורות also needs inspection, from 'ועבדת את העבודה הזאת'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the later פסח also needs inspection. The פסוק 'you shall do this service in this month' makes every later פסח like the first. So הזה cannot be excluding later פסחים from inspection.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסח of later generations also needs inspection. It is written: 'You shall do this service in this month.' This teaches that all the services of this month should be like this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its answer. Just as the תמיד has its own source for inspection, a separate פסוק teaches that later פסחים follow the פסח of מצרים, so they also need the four-day inspection. This sets up the next step, which says what הזה excludes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד's inspection comes from תשמרו, and פסח דורות gets its inspection from ועבדת את העבודה הזאת, which links it to פסח מצרים. Since both have their own sources, the word הזה in 'until the fourteenth of this month' is not needed to teach inspection, and it does not exclude later פסחים. It must exclude something else, and the next step says what.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסח brought every year in later generations, as opposed to the one in מצרים
Also, too
'You shall do this service.' Teaches that later פסחים follow the first one
Like this one. All later services must match this one

steps.confusionAlert: This פסוק makes later פסחים match the first one in inspection. It does not cancel step 9. Taking the lamb on the tenth is still only for מצרים, because the פסוק there says הזה.

phrases.english: And the Pesach of later generations too,
surely it is written: 'And you shall perform this service'

phrases.english: in this month,'

phrases.english: meaning that all the services of this month should be like this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer of step 12. Like the תמיד, פסח דורות has its own source for inspection (ועבדת), which leaves הזה free for a different job (step 14).
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea from step 10 that הזה in 'until the fourteenth of this month' might limit inspection to פסח מצרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ועבדת את העבודה הזאת makes later פסחים follow the first one, including inspection. So הזה cannot be excluding פסח דורות from inspection.

steps.title: The word הזה excludes פסח שני from the four-day inspection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that הזה in 'guard it until the fourteenth of this month' excludes פסח שני. פסח שני is similar to פסח מצרים, but it does not need a four-day inspection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that word 'this' comes to exclude פסח שני, which is similar to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The word הזה does not exclude later פסחים. It excludes פסח שני from the four-day inspection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since פסח דורות needs inspection, הזה needs a different job. פסח שני is like פסח מצרים in some ways, such as lasting only one day. So we might have thought it needs inspection too. The word הזה teaches that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Drops the earlier idea and offers a new explanation
To exclude. A word that comes to leave a case out of a rule
The make-up פסח on 14 אייר for those who could not bring it in ניסן
Which is similar to it

steps.whatToRemember: The four-day inspection applies to פסח מצרים and to every later פסח in ניסן (because of 'ועבדת את העבודה הזאת'), and also to the תמיד (because of תשמרו). The word הזה in 'until the fourteenth of this month' leaves out only פסח שני. In contrast, taking the lamb on the tenth was only for מצרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה: פסח ראשון in every generation needs a four-day inspection, but פסח שני does not.

phrases.english: Rather, that word 'this' —
comes to exclude the second Pesach, which is similar to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of steps 12–13. Since the תמיד and פסח דורות get inspection from other sources, the word הזה is left to exclude פסח שני.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the drasha: the word is moved to exclude a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הזה in 'until the fourteenth of this month' limits the four-day inspection to פסח מצרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every פסח in ניסן needs inspection. הזה only excludes פסח שני, which is similar to פסח מצרים, from needing a four-day inspection.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The four-day inspection applies to every פסח ראשון. Only פסח שני is exempt, because of the word הזה.

steps.title: Would 'this night' mean only פסח מצרים is eaten at night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading of הזה as a limit. If it were a limit, then 'eat the meat on this night' would mean only פסח מצרים must be eaten at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to this approach, the פסוק says 'And they shall eat the meat on this night.' Would we also say that only this פסח is eaten at night, and no other פסח is eaten at night?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק that also uses the word הזה. It shows that reading הזה as a limit leads to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 read הזה as limiting a rule to פסח מצרים alone. Applying the same method here would mean later פסחים do not have to be eaten at night. Everyone knows that is false, so the method itself is under attack.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if that is so (opens a challenge that pushes a logic to an absurd result)
'And they shall eat the meat on this night' (שמות יב:ח)
So too? (Would we really say this?)
Another one (here, a later פסח)

phrases.english: But now, according to this, that which is written:
"And they shall eat the meat on this night",
so too, would this one be eaten at night,
phrases.notes: 'This one' means פסח מצרים.

phrases.english: and no other is eaten at night?!
phrases.notes: Of course not: every פסח is eaten at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to challenge the derivation of step 9, where הזה was read as limiting a rule to פסח מצרים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the word הזה limits a law to פסח מצרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum. The same word in the eating פסוק would free later פסחים from being eaten at night, which is clearly wrong.

steps.title: 'You shall do this service' extends the night rule to every פסח
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ועבדת את העבודה' teaches that later פסחים follow the laws of פסח מצרים. So they too are eaten at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall do this service.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with the same פסוק it used in step 13. That פסוק makes every later פסח like the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night rule for later פסחים does not rest on the word הזה. It comes from ועבדת, which carries the laws of the first פסח into all later generations. So the word הזה cannot take that rule away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall do this service' (שמות יג:ה). It makes later פסחים like פסח מצרים.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And you shall do this service."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a separate פסוק that extends the law, which outweighs any limit implied by the word הזה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word הזה might restrict eating at night to פסח מצרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: ועבדת makes every later פסח follow the laws of the first, so it too is eaten at night.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'this' night?
steps.stepSummary: If ועבדת already makes all פסחים alike, the word הזה in the eating פסוק seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the word 'this'?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 16 creates a new problem. Now the word הזה seems to have no job, so the גמרא asks what it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not use extra words without a reason. Since הזה does not limit the law to פסח מצרים, it must teach something else. The גמרא is setting up its next answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks what an apparently extra word teaches)

phrases.english: Rather, why do I need "this"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 16, which left הזה without a job.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word הזה in 'בלילה הזה' comes to teach.

steps.title: 'This' is used for the time-limit teachings of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The word הזה is needed for the teachings of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא about the time for eating the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for the teaching of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the word הזה a real job. It points to a known מחלוקת about how late the פסח may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ברכות ט. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה compares 'this night' here to 'this night' when ה׳ passed through Egypt. He learns from this that the פסח may be eaten only until midnight. רבי עקיבא uses הזה to teach that the פסח is eaten at night and not by day. Either way, הזה has its own purpose and is not a limit to פסח מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: For the teaching of רבי...
A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: The two תנאים do not use הזה for the same teaching. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses it to set a midnight deadline. רבי עקיבא uses it to rule out eating by day. Both agree, though, that it is not a limit to פסח מצרים.

phrases.aramaic: לְכִדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: For the teaching of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya and Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: See ברכות ט.: midnight versus dawn as the deadline for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הזה is used for the time-limit teachings: until midnight according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, or only at night and not by day according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Would 'from it' mean a ערל may eat a later פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge comes back with the word בו. If 'no ערל shall eat from it' limits the ban to פסח מצרים, a ערל could eat a later פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to this approach, the פסוק says 'And no uncircumcised man shall eat from it.' Would we also say that only from 'it' he may not eat, but he may eat from the פסח of later generations?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the limiting-word method a second time, now with the word בו. Read as a limit, it would allow a ערל to eat a later פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like step 15, only with a different limiting word. If בו restricts the ban on a ערל to פסח מצרים, the ban would not apply to later פסחים. That result is clearly wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncircumcised man
'And no uncircumcised man shall eat from it' (שמות יב:מח)
The פסח of later generations (every year after Egypt)

phrases.english: But now, according to this, that which is written:
"And no uncircumcised man shall eat from it",
so too, would it be that from "it" he does not eat,
but he does eat from the Pesach of later generations?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה דִּכְתִיב: ״וְכׇל עָרֵל לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel challenge to step 15, now using the word בו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of reading limiting words in the פסוקים of פסח מצרים as excluding later פסחים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum. The word בו would allow a ערל to eat a later פסח, which is clearly wrong.

steps.title: 'You shall do' extends the ban on a ערל to every פסח
steps.stepSummary: Again, ועבדת teaches that later פסחים follow the laws of פסח מצרים. So a ערל may not eat any פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as in step 16. ועבדת makes every later פסח like the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a ערל eating a later פסח comes from ועבדת. So the word בו cannot remove that ban.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall do' (short reference to the same פסוק as in step 16)

phrases.english: The verse says: "And you shall do."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19, using the same answer as step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate פסוק extends the law to later generations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word בו might limit the ban on a ערל to פסח מצרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: ועבדת applies the ban on a ערל to every פסח.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'from it'?
steps.stepSummary: If ועבדת already covers later פסחים, the word בו seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need 'from it'?
steps.whatsHappening: As in step 17, the גמרא asks what the extra word now teaches. It is setting up its final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בו does not separate פסח מצרים from later פסחים. So it must be excluding something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From it' (here, the פסח)

phrases.english: Rather, why do I need "from it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 20, which left בו without a job.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word בו comes to exclude.

steps.title: A ערל is barred only from the פסח, not from מצה and מרור
steps.stepSummary: The word בו teaches that a ערל is barred only from the פסח. He still eats מצה and מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: From 'it' he may not eat, but he does eat מצה and מרור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that בו limits the ban to the פסח itself. It does not limit the ban to פסח מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the word בו, we might think a ערל is cut off from all the eating מצוות of the night. בו tells us the ban covers only the קרבן פסח. A ערל is still obligated to eat מצה and מרור like every other Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Unleavened bread, which every Jew must eat on the night of פסח
Bitter herbs

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern of this section is that a limiting word in the פסוקים of פסח מצרים does not cut off later פסחים, because ועבדת makes them all alike. Each limiting word still teaches something else. הזה is used for the time limit for eating the פסח. בו teaches that a ערל is barred only from the פסח and still eats מצה and מרור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical הלכה. A ערל is obligated in מצה and מרור, even though he may not eat the קרבן פסח.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mistake what בו limits. It narrows the ban to which food is forbidden (the פסח, not מצה and מרור). It does not narrow which year's פסח the ban applies to.

phrases.english: That from "it" he does not eat,
but he does eat matzah and bitter herbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּ״בוֹ״ אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל, אֲבָל הוּא אוֹכֵל בְּמַצָּה וּמָרוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בו limits the ban on a ערל to the פסח itself, so he still eats מצה and מרור.

steps.title: Does 'from it' limit the ban on a בן נכר to the Egyptian פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge is now raised about the בן נכר verse: maybe בו means he is barred only from פסח מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, when the verse says 'No stranger shall eat from it', should we also say that only from 'it' (the Egyptian פסח) he may not eat, but he may eat the פסח of later generations?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same challenge it raised about the ערל. This time it is about a בן נכר, someone estranged from ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says a בן נכר shall not eat 'בו' (from it). Just as before, one could read 'it' narrowly as the פסח in Egypt only. That reading would allow a בן נכר to eat the פסח in later years.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (introduces a challenge built on the previous logic)
A 'stranger'; here, a Jew who is estranged from ה׳ (an apostate)
The פסח offered in all later generations

steps.confusionAlert: Here בן נכר does not mean a non-Jew. The גמרא understands it as a Jew who has become estranged from ה׳, a משומד.

phrases.english: But if so:
'No stranger shall eat from it',
so too, is it only 'from it' that he does not eat,
but he does eat the פסח of later generations?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the challenge from step 19 to a new verse, the one about בן נכר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of בו in the בן נכר verse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בו narrows the subject to the Egyptian פסח, then a בן נכר would be allowed to eat later פסחים.

steps.title: ועבדת extends the ban to all generations
steps.stepSummary: The word ועבדת teaches that later פסחים follow the rules of פסח מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And you shall perform (this service).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with ועבדת. It teaches that every later פסח has the same rules as the one in Egypt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since later פסחים copy the laws of פסח מצרים, a בן נכר is barred from every פסח. So בו cannot be used to limit the ban to Egypt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall perform': the rules of the Egyptian פסח carry over to later generations

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And you shall perform.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a separate verse that overrides the narrow reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בו limits the ban on a בן נכר to פסח מצרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of ועבדת, a בן נכר is barred from every פסח.

steps.title: What is the word 'from it' for?
steps.stepSummary: If ועבדת covers later פסחים, the word בו in the בן נכר verse seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the word 'from it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what בו teaches now that it no longer limits the ban to Egypt. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words. Since בו is not narrowing the ban to פסח מצרים, it must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks for the purpose of a word)

phrases.english: But then, why do I need 'from it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 24, which left בו without a job.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the word בו in the בן נכר verse

steps.title: Being an apostate bars the פסח but not תרומה
steps.stepSummary: בו teaches that a משומד is disqualified from the פסח, but not from eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From it': apostasy disqualifies a person from eating the פסח. But apostasy does not disqualify a person from eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בו limits this ban to the פסח alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who became a משומד may not eat the פסח. The word בו ('from it', meaning the פסח) shows that the ban does not spread to other holy food. So he may still eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Apostasy; being a Jew who has abandoned the Torah
Disqualifies
The holy produce portion given to כהנים

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule. A כהן who is a משומד keeps his right to eat תרומה, even though he may not eat the פסח.

phrases.english: 'From it', apostasy disqualifies,
but apostasy does not disqualify from תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בו limits the apostate's disqualification to the פסח only, and excludes תרומה.

steps.title: Why the Torah wrote both ערל and בן נכר
steps.stepSummary: Each ban teaches something the other could not, so both had to be written.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write 'uncircumcised', and it was necessary to write 'stranger'. If the Torah had written only 'uncircumcised', I would say he is barred because a foreskin is repulsive, but a stranger is not repulsive, so I would say he may eat. That is why it was needed. And if the Torah had taught only 'stranger', I would say he is barred because his heart is not directed to Heaven, but an uncircumcised person whose heart is directed to Heaven, I would say may eat. That is why it was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the Torah needed two separate bans, one on the ערל and one on the בן נכר. Each has its own reason, so one cannot be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערל is barred because of a physical flaw: the foreskin is considered repulsive. The בן נכר is barred because of a spiritual flaw: his heart is turned away from Heaven. Since each reason is missing in the other case, we could not learn one ban from the other, so the Torah wrote both.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
An uncircumcised man
Repulsive, disgusting
His heart is directed toward Heaven
It is needed (a צריכותא: showing each case is necessary)

steps.whatToRemember: ערל = barred for a physical reason (מאיס). בן נכר = barred for a spiritual reason (אין לבו לשמים). Neither can be learned from the other.
steps.confusionAlert: The ערל discussed here is a Jew whose heart is to Heaven, such as someone whose brothers died from מילה. He is not uncircumcised out of rebellion. That is why his heart is called 'to Heaven'.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write 'uncircumcised',
and it was necessary to write 'stranger'.
For if the Torah had written only 'uncircumcised',
that is because he is repulsive,
but a stranger is not repulsive,
so I would say no ban; therefore it was needed.
And if it had taught us only 'stranger',
that is because his heart is not toward Heaven,
but an uncircumcised man, whose heart is toward Heaven,
I would say no ban; therefore it was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having discussed both the ערל and בן נכר verses, the גמרא explains why both were needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both bans are needed because each rests on a different reason: physical repulsiveness versus a heart turned from Heaven.

steps.title: Does 'from it' limit the ban on a תושב and שכיר to Egypt?
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge is raised a third time, now about the תושב and the שכיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, when the verse says 'A sojourner and a hired servant shall not eat from it', should we say only from 'it' he may not eat, but he may eat the פסח of later generations?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same challenge again, this time about the verse of the תושב and שכיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This verse also uses the word בו. One could again read it as limiting the ban to the פסח in Egypt.

keyTerms.meaning: A sojourner, resident
A hired worker
The פסח of later generations

phrases.english: But if so:
'A sojourner and a hired servant shall not eat from it',

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּ״בוֹ״ הוּא אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: so too, is it only 'from it' that he does not eat,
but he does eat from the פסח of later generations?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה: ״תּוֹשָׁב וְשָׂכִיר לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the בו pattern and applies it to a third verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of בו in the תושב ושכיר verse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בו narrows the ban to the Egyptian פסח, then a תושב and שכיר could eat later פסחים.

steps.title: Again ועבדת extends the ban
steps.stepSummary: ועבדת makes the Egyptian rules apply in every generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And you shall perform.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: ועבדת carries the ban into all later פסחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later פסחים follow the laws of פסח מצרים. So the תושב and שכיר are barred from every פסח.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And you shall perform.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a separate verse that overrides the narrow reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בו limits the ban on a תושב and שכיר to פסח מצרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of ועבדת, the ban applies to every פסח.

steps.title: Again, what is 'from it' for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בו adds in the תושב ושכיר verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need 'from it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the purpose of בו in this verse. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ועבדת already extends the ban to later generations, בו must have another job here too.

phrases.english: But then, why do I need 'from it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 29, which left בו without a job.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of בו in the תושב ושכיר verse

steps.title: Same answer: apostasy bars the פסח, not תרומה
steps.stepSummary: בו again teaches that being a משומד disqualifies from the פסח but not from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From it': apostasy disqualifies a person from eating the פסח. But apostasy does not disqualify a person from eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave for the בן נכר verse. This closes the pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on the פסח is limited by the word בו to the פסח alone. A disqualification like משומדות does not spread to תרומה.
steps.whatToRemember: Across all these verses, ועבדת makes the bans apply to every פסח. Each בו is used for a separate teaching: the ערל still eats מצה and מרור, and a משומד still eats תרומה.

phrases.english: 'From it', apostasy disqualifies,
but apostasy does not disqualify from תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30 by repeating the answer of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בו limits the apostate's disqualification to the פסח and excludes תרומה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The limiting word בו never restricts the bans to פסח מצרים. Instead, it limits each ban to the פסח itself.

steps.title: Does the circumcision rule apply only in Egypt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: maybe the rule that a man's household must be circumcised before he eats applied only to פסח מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the verse says, "When you have circumcised him, then he shall eat of it." Should we also say that only of 'it' (פסח מצרים) he may not eat, but he may eat of פסח דורות?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same pattern of attack a fourth time. Now the target is the verse about circumcising one's household before eating the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בו seems to point to one specific פסח, the one in Egypt. If so, maybe a man with uncircumcised sons or slaves could eat later פסחים. The גמרא finds this hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now (introduces a challenge from an unwanted result)
Should we say so too?
And you shall circumcise him
The פסח brought in later generations

but he does eat of the פסח of later generations?!

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that בו limits a rule to פסח מצרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בו limits rules to Egypt, then the circumcision requirement would not apply to later generations, which cannot be right.

steps.title: ועבדת carries the circumcision rule forward
steps.stepSummary: The verse ועבדת extends the rule to every generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And you shall perform (this service)."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. The word ועבדת tells us the Egyptian rules apply in all generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ועבדת makes the practice in Egypt the model for every later פסח. So the circumcision requirement applies to פסח דורות too.

keyTerms.meaning: "And you shall perform" (Exodus 13:5)

phrases.english: The verse says: "And you shall perform."

steps.title: So what does בו teach here?
steps.stepSummary: If ועבדת already covers all generations, why is בו written?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do I need "of it"?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the word בו did not limit the rule to Egypt, the גמרא asks what job it does. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words. So בו must teach some other point.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it?

phrases.english: But why do I need "of it"?

steps.title: Household circumcision holds back פסח but not תרומה
steps.stepSummary: בו teaches that uncircumcised sons and slaves stop a man from eating פסח but not from eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Of it": the circumcision of his males and his slaves holds him back from it, but the circumcision of his males and slaves does not hold him back from תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that בו limits the rule to פסח. A man whose sons or slaves are not circumcised may not eat the פסח, but he may still eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the limit set by בו is about which קרבן the rule covers, not which generation. This rule about one's household is special to פסח. A כהן whose household is not circumcised still eats his תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: The circumcision of his male children and his slaves
Holds back, prevents
The priestly portion of produce eaten by כהנים

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בו limits the household circumcision rule to פסח and leaves תרומה out
steps.confusionAlert: This is about the circumcision of a man's sons and slaves, not his own. A man who is himself uncircumcised may not eat תרומה either. The point here is only that his household's status does not block him from תרומה.

steps.title: Was breaking a bone forbidden only in Egypt?
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge is raised about the ban on breaking a bone, which is also written with בו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, it is written: "And they shall not break a bone in it." Should we also say that of 'it' one does not break a bone, but one may break a bone of פסח דורות?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same pattern to the ban on breaking a bone of the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too the verse uses בו. If בו pointed to Egypt alone, it would be allowed to break bones of later פסחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Bone
They shall not break

phrases.english: But if so, that which is written:
"And they shall not break a bone in it,"

but one does break a bone of the פסח of later generations?!

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that בו limits the bone ban to פסח מצרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בו limits rules to Egypt, bone breaking would be allowed in later generations, which cannot be right.

steps.title: ועבדת carries the bone ban forward
steps.stepSummary: ועבדת again extends the rule to every generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And you shall perform."
steps.whatsHappening: Same answer: ועבדת makes the ban on breaking a bone apply to every later פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The model of פסח מצרים, including the bone ban, carries over to פסח דורות.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking a bone (the name of this prohibition)

phrases.english: The verse says: "And you shall perform."

steps.terutzMaskana: The bone ban applies to פסח דורות

steps.title: What does בו teach about bones?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what job בו does in the bone verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why do I need "in it"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking what the extra word בו teaches here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ועבדת already covers the generations question, so בו must teach a different limit.

keyTerms.meaning: "In it" or "of it", a word that narrows a rule

phrases.english: But why do I need "in it"?

steps.title: The bone ban covers only a כשר פסח
steps.stepSummary: בו teaches that the ban applies only to a valid פסח, not to a פסול one.
steps.simpleTranslation: "In it": in a כשר one, and not in a פסול one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בו limits the bone ban to a valid פסח. Breaking a bone of a disqualified פסח is not forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the limit set by בו is about which animal, not which generation. A פסח that became פסול is still a פסח in name, but this particular ban does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid, fit to be eaten as a קרבן
Disqualified

phrases.english: "In it": in a valid one, and not in a disqualified one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bone ban applies only to a כשר פסח

steps.title: Was raw meat forbidden only in Egypt?
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is raised again about eating the פסח raw, a verse written with ממנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, it is written: "Do not eat of it raw." Of 'it' you may not eat raw, but you may eat raw meat of פסח דורות?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא runs the same challenge on the ban against eating the פסח raw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word here is ממנו ("of it"), and it seems to narrow the rule in the same way. If so, raw eating would be allowed in later generations.

Of it
Do not eat

steps.title: ועבדת carries the raw-meat ban forward

steps.whatsHappening: Same answer once more: ועבדת makes the ban on eating it raw apply forever.

steps.title: What does ממנו teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the word ממנו is written.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ממנו does not limit the rule to Egypt, it must be written for another teaching.

steps.title: ממנו is needed for the teaching of רבה in the name of רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: ממנו is used for a גזירה שוה taught by רבה in the name of רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for that which רבה said in the name of רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ממנו is needed for a known teaching of רבה quoting רבי יצחק. The גמרא only mentions it here and does not spell it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That teaching (found in יבמות) links the word ממנו here to the word ממנו said about מעשר, using a גזירה שוה. It teaches that an ערל may not eat מעשר, just as he may not eat the פסח. So ממנו has its own job and is not limiting the rule to Egypt.

keyTerms.meaning: For that which רבה taught
A link between two verses that share the same word
An uncircumcised man

steps.whatToRemember: In all these verses, ועבדת brings the Egyptian rules into every generation. Each narrowing word (בו or ממנו) teaches a different limit: the household circumcision rule does not cover תרומה, the bone ban covers only a כשר פסח, and ממנו is used for the גזירה שוה of רבה in the name of רבי יצחק.

phrases.english: For that which רבה said in the name of רבי יצחק.

steps.title: Source for eating in haste only in Egypt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line that פסח מצרים was eaten in haste, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And it is eaten in haste," etc. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote the next line of the משנה. It asks for the source that only פסח מצרים had to be eaten in haste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the rules of פסח מצרים carried over to later generations. Eating in haste is different, since the משנה says it applied only in Egypt. So the גמרא needs a source for this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Haste, hurry
From where do we know?
Etcetera (the rest of the quoted line)

steps.title: אותו: only the Egyptian פסח is eaten in haste
steps.stepSummary: The word אותו limits eating in haste to פסח מצרים alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the verse says: "And you shall eat it in haste." "It" is eaten in haste, and no other is eaten in haste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the verse "and you shall eat it in haste." The word אותו teaches that only that פסח was eaten in haste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the narrowing word does limit the rule to Egypt. ועבדת does not undo it, because אותו is written right on this rule. So פסח דורות is still a פסח in every way, but this one detail does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: It (that one)
Another (here: any other פסח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that not every Egyptian rule carries forward. Where the Torah clearly narrows the rule, as with אותו for eating in haste, it stays a one-time feature of פסח מצרים.
steps.whatToRemember: Eating in haste was required only for פסח מצרים, learned from אותו in "ואכלתם אותו בחפזון."

steps.title: What does 'applies all seven days' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that פסח דורות applies all seven days and asks what this line is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And פסח דורות applies all seven days, etc.' On what does this statement stand? In other words, what is it talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה and asks what the phrase 'applies all seven days' is talking about. This question sets up the next move, where the גמרא tests a possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say clearly what 'applies' for seven days. It could mean the קרבן פסח itself, or it could mean a law connected to פסח, such as the ban on חמץ. The גמרא asks which one the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסח kept in all later generations, not the one in מצרים
Applies, is in effect
All seven days of the יום טוב

steps.title: It cannot mean the קרבן פסח itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the reading that the phrase means the קרבן פסח and rejects it, since the קרבן פסח is not brought for seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the קרבן פסח itself, is there a קרבן פסח for all seven days? There is not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, that 'applies all seven days' means the קרבן פסח, and shows right away that this cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח is brought only on the fourteenth of ניסן and eaten that night. So it makes no sense to say the קרבן 'applies all seven days.' This pushes the גמרא to look for a different meaning for the משנה's words.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, if we suggest
On the Pesach, meaning the קרבן פסח itself
Is there? A question that expects the answer 'no'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'מי איכא' as a real question looking for information. It is a rhetorical challenge, and the obvious answer is 'no.' There is no קרבן פסח on all seven days.

phrases.english: If we say it refers to the Paschal lamb,
is there a Paschal lamb all seven days?!
phrases.notes: Of course not: the קרבן is brought only on the fourteenth of ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tests the first possible answer to the question 'אמאי קאי' and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'נוהג כל שבעה' refers to the קרבן פסח itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קרבן פסח is brought only on one day, the fourteenth of ניסן, so it cannot be said to apply for seven days.
